tagline: Skin science grown from a single plant
descriptor: Korean derma cosmetics built on a patented Ageratum extract: eight products for dry, sensitive and itch-prone skin, four patents and papers in peer-reviewed scientific journals
about: AGERA BioTech is a Korean company that grew out of a university laboratory. It was founded in 2016 by Professor SoonYoung Shin, a researcher with more than thirty years in the life sciences and a lecturer at Konkuk University. She studied the plant Ageratum houstonianum, known in Korean as 불로화, and found that its extract has a marked effect on skin recovery and hydration. The company patented that property and then launched the AGERIN brand.

The brand rests on a foundation unusual for cosmetics: not a marketing story, but papers in peer-reviewed journals. The company named the active compound isolated from the extract Agerarin, and work on it has appeared in Scientific Reports, PNAS, Journal of Dermatological Science and Molecules. Such a set of references is rare for a cosmetics brand, and for a buyer with a scientific team it provides what is usually missing: a source that can be checked.

The range is narrow and built around a single task. Eight products cover a full daily routine, from cleansing to sun care, and all of them are intended for skin that is dry, sensitive and prone to irritation and itching. The company notes separately that its flagship cream is suitable for children, pregnant women and people with very dry skin.

The company describes its own approach as derma cosmetics: products for daily use, not medical preparations. The test results, percentages and patent numbers given below are the company's data. Documents and protocols are provided separately, for a specific market or a specific buyer.

lines.name: AGERIN
lines.note: The brand's only line, and that is the point of it: eight products are built around one active compound and complement each other in a daily routine. Cleansing is covered by a cream-to-foam cleanser, no-rinse cotton pads and an exfoliating gel that works on the proteins of the stratum corneum instead of using abrasives. Hydration and overnight recovery are handled by an essence toner and a night mask, applied before sleep and left on. Barrier and itching are handled by the rich ABC cream for face and body and a spot cream for damaged areas. The day is closed by a hybrid sunscreen, SPF 50+ PA++++. In six of the eight products the company states a cooling complex, Soothing Cooler; the patent for it belongs not to the company itself but to its contract manufacturer.

tech.name: Ageratum and Agerarin
tech.note: The plant Ageratum houstonianum means “ageless” in Greek, and in Korean it is called 불로화, the flower of longevity. The company isolated an active compound from its extract and named it Agerarin. The first paper on it appeared in Scientific Reports in 2017 (7:11175). This is the brand's proprietary compound, and it is present in all eight products of the line.

tech.name: Aquaporin-3 and the skin's daily clock
tech.note: The mechanism as the company describes it. Skin that has dried out and been damaged during the day recovers at night through the work of clock genes. Agerarin affects this daily rhythm and, through it, the protein aquaporin-3, which carries water and glycerol into the epidermis. Glycerol holds moisture and takes part in the synthesis of ceramides, which make up the skin barrier. The night mask is built on the same mechanism: the company recommends applying it between 22:00 and 06:00.

tech.name: Four patents
tech.note: The company lists four registered Korean patents: 10-1815340 for a composition containing Ageratum extract, 10-1784331 for a compound that increases aquaporin-3 expression, 10-2142210 for an anti-atopy composition acting through increased filaggrin, and 10-2107748 for an anti-itch composition based on a complex of Ageratum, Schisandra and Bupleurum. Patent 10-1525752, which covers the cooling component in the sunscreen, belongs not to AGERA BioTech but to its contract manufacturer: the company clarified this separately. The numbers are given as stated in the company's materials.

tech.name: Papers in scientific journals
tech.note: Beyond Scientific Reports, the company refers to papers in Journal of Dermatological Science (2018), Journal of Food and Drug Analysis (2020), Molecular Biology Reports (2021), Molecules (2022 and 2024) and PNAS (2022). The topics cover hydration, restoration of filaggrin and the skin barrier, tone brightening, and action against wrinkles and itching. A 2026 paper in the International Journal of Molecular Sciences addresses hair growth.

tech.name: Human trials
tech.note: For the ABC cream the company reports the results of a human trial: skin hydration rose by 76.26% and itch intensity fell by an average of 46.48% after four weeks of use. For the exfoliating gel it reports a clinical study dated 22 July 2025 with twenty female participants: the keratinised cell measure changed by 36.65% and skin roughness by 15.50%. The study was carried out by the independent laboratory Global Standard Certification Co., Ltd. These are the company's data; protocols are provided at the deal stage.

tech.name: Soothing Cooler
tech.note: A cooling complex based on plant extracts: Ulmus davidiana, aloe vera, Dioscorea japonica, laminaria and Viola mandshurica. It gives a sensation of coolness immediately on application. The patents for this complex and for the cooling component in the sunscreen belong to AGERA BioTech's contract manufacturer, not to the company itself.

formats: Cream-to-foam cleanser and cotton pads for cleansing
exportNote: The company states that its products are registered for the European Union through the CPNP system, for the USA under MoCRA requirements, and also in Vietnam and Myanmar. The trademark is registered in the USA. The products are sold in Korea through duty-free stores and online, and outside Korea in Japan, Vietnam and on international marketplaces. The company currently has no appointed distributors in Latin or North America: it confirmed this in writing on 14 September 2026, and both markets are open.

catalog_notes: A rich cream for dry, sensitive and itch-prone skin, which the company presents as a product for the whole family: from face to feet, for children and pregnant women. It is built on a high concentration of Ageratum extract, patent 10-2107748. According to the company, four weeks of use raised hydration by 76.26% and reduced itching by an average of 46.48%.

A spot cream for areas with a damaged barrier. It forms a non-sticky protective film and is intended for dry, flaking and itchy areas, as well as for irritation after hair removal or radiation therapy. The formula is plant-based, and the company states it can be used on infants and pregnant women.

A light, watery essence toner without a heavy texture. It absorbs quickly, leaves no stickiness and works as a base for the rest of the routine. Suitable for all skin types, primarily sensitive and combination. Patents 10-1815340 and 10-1784331.

A night mask applied to a cleansed face before sleep and left on. The company recommends using it between 22:00 and 06:00, when the skin recovers most actively. Alongside Ageratum, the formula contains Schisandra and Bupleurum extracts.

A hybrid sunscreen, SPF 50+ PA++++, combining mineral and chemical filters. The texture is hydrating and leaves no white cast, so the product also works under make-up. The cooling component is covered by patent 10-1525752, which belongs to the contract manufacturer.

Cotton pads for no-rinse cleansing, fifty per pack. The fabric is 100% cotton, certified to OEKO-TEX STANDARD 100 in product class I, that is, to the requirements for baby articles. They remove make-up, including waterproof, and contain moringa seed oil.

An exfoliating gel that, instead of abrasive particles, binds the proteins of the stratum corneum and removes only keratinised cells. The formula also contains an enzyme complex and plant extracts for the skin microbiome. The clinical study results are given above.

A cleanser that is applied like a cream and turns into a dense micro-foam. It cleanses without leaving the skin tight, and contains a plant complex for sebum and pores together with the company's cooling complex.
